messageTrail.text: I’ll inspect the shipping service setup and existing module dependencies first, then patch the gRPC server wiring without running a build.
The checkout service already has current OpenTelemetry wiring, so I’m going to mirror that pattern in shipping to stay consistent with the repo.

Shipping already has the OpenTelemetry packages in its module graph indirectly, but the trace SDK/exporter imports need to become explicit for this service. I’m patching only the service source and dependency metadata.

The checkout dependency versions are newer than shipping’s current module file, so I’m keeping shipping aligned with its own existing OpenTelemetry versions instead of broadening the dependency change.
I’m going to make tracing setup return a shutdown function so the SDK can flush on process exit, and wire the otelgrpc server stats handler when tracing is enabled.
The first patch exposed one necessary signature change for initTracing; I’m correcting that and then I’ll format and check the affected files without building.
I’m formatting the changed Go file now. After that I’ll update module metadata so the new imports are declared explicitly.
gofmt is not on PATH in this environment. I’ll keep the import block in standard order manually and still inspect the final diff for syntax-level issues.

Since Go is not installed on PATH here, I can’t ask the toolchain to regenerate sums. I found matching checksums already present in sibling services and will copy only the needed module entries into shipping’s go.sum.

I’m updating go.mod by moving the newly imported OpenTelemetry modules into the direct require block and adding the trace exporter/SDK packages at the same version already used in shipping’s module graph.
Next I’m adding the corresponding checksum entries from sibling module files, because the local Go toolchain isn’t available to do that mechanically.
The trace exporter pulls in a couple of OTLP modules that weren’t previously needed by shipping, so I’m adding those sums alongside the existing OpenTelemetry entries.
The code and module files are patched. I’m doing a final diff/read-through now; I won’t run go build or any command that builds the package.

The final diff shows the intended wiring. I’m checking whether the exporter’s transitive modules already have sums in shipping so the committed metadata is complete enough without a local go mod tidy.

Shipping lacks two checksum entries that the OTLP exporter commonly brings in. I’m adding those as indirect requirements as well, to keep the module file explicit and avoid leaving that cleanup for the next Go command.
Now I’m adding the matching sums for those indirect modules from the existing sibling service files.
The first checksum patch missed because shipping’s go.sum has different existing hashes around that location. I’ve read the local file and am applying a narrower patch against the actual lines.
That patch also hit a nearby mismatch, so I’m splitting the checksum additions into smaller hunks against exact anchors.
The dependency metadata is complete enough for the new imports. I’m doing one last targeted read for line references and to confirm no build command was run.
The diff check passes for whitespace. Go commands are unavailable on PATH here, so I could not run gofmt or dependency regeneration; I did not run go build.

Implemented OpenTelemetry tracing for src/shippingservice/main.go. What changed: Added otelgrpc.NewServerHandler() to the gRPC server when tracing is enabled. Initialized an OTLP gRPC trace exporter using COLLECTOR_ADDR. Set the OpenTelemetry tracer provider with the Go SDK and an always-sample batcher. Added trace-context and baggage propagation. Added shutdown flushing for the tracer provider. U
